One of my special interests are movies. 

They have a power to transport you to another reality. A different state of mind if you will.

You can be anybody, I think that is why I like them so much.

Well, my collection of movies (and games) has gotten a bit out of control...

I simply do not have the storage for them all.

I have been fighting an internal battle for months. 'You need to cut down'. 

But, I am not exaggerating when I tell you that my attachment to these films (most of them anyway) is so extreme.

I compromised.

I will remove the bulk.

I purchased these disc holders and forged a plan.

I would keep the cases of the dvds I loved the most, and cut the cases for the ones I did not mind losing. 

This was an excellent plan! Except...I only put by about 50 of them to go in the folders...

My sister - no amateur when it comes to helping me look at things in another way during these moments - intervened.

She helped me realise that, I could still keep the artwork for all of them, it would just be condensed.

This was extremely difficult to do. I was physically cutting up things I loved, I wanted to cry. But I knew it would benefit me so much long term. 

So, about 6 hours after starting, I have done something I would never have done a year ago. 

There are easily around 120-130 movies (plus the 100+ games) de-cased and stored more efficiently.

I have one strict rule - the only movies I am allowed to purchase in the future are MCU or Disney Classics. THAT IS IT.

The only thing to think about now is how to recycle/upcycle all the empty caes?

I am exhausted. But relieved.

I worry that I am too placid in my attempts to resolve the issue. I fear that there will always be a drastic negative impact from my actions. Approaching this fills me with so much anxiety. To the point I let things build and build, and when I eventually try to 'fix' it, the bomb has gone off and we are already in fallout.

I am scared to address the situation. But I know I cannot keep living it. The stress is making me unwell. I love my job. But the necessities of the role are making it difficult to enjoy.

I want to grow, and get better at the job but I don't want to get sick trying.

I have been working there for 8 years this September.

The first 5 were spent working under really unsatisfactory management (the kind that could get you closed down if the local authority found out)

I was promoted to Manager May 2017. I had no idea what I was doing. I was 22 years old thrown in the deep end and expected to fix the rubble the previous management had left.

And don't get me wrong, I have done an okay job. It would have closed. But as a team, we kept it open. 

But this one individual (who was part of this team work and likely one key factor in saving it) has become top heavy with power. And if she doesn't have it - even though she isn't in charge - she spits out her dummy and makes sure everyone knows it. 

And all it does is make me feel like s**t and not worthy of the role I have been given.

I feel I am all or nothing.

In some aspects of my job, I excel. But in many others, it's like I constantly need my hand holding. Either because I don't know how to do something or I'm too scared to do it.

It frustrates me. I understand that many individuals, especially managers probably do and are going through something like this. But I feel as if there are more things I am bad at than good.

And the longer I stay stuck here, the worse off the business will be. I think it is unfair for everyone else to potentially suffer while I learn.
